description:
FILED s539b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-16) from a port-4 probe (scratch/s539b/pr/s3.pl in the s539b worktree).  PRE-EXISTING on main c1fe4930.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3):

    my $a = 5; my @b = (7, 8);
    use feature 'signatures'; no warnings; sub f ($x = $a, $y = $b[1]) { return "f=$x/$y" }
    print f(), " ", f(1, 2), "\n";                 # perl: f=5/8 f=1/2     main: f=/8 f=1/2
    { my $a = 6; use feature 'signatures'; my $g = sub ($z = $a) { "g=$z" }; print $g->(), "\n"; }   # g=6

The feature pragma on the sub's own line makes PPI hand the signature over as ONE Token::Prototype (#455).  `my $a` is an exception-partition name, renamed `$a__excl__0`; the region walk (_rename_decl_within -> _rename_use_token) had no arm for a Prototype token, so the default kept `$a` and read the special.  The binder records the default's uses at the token (Binder::_proto_params), so the port's rename (_rename_binding: exactly uses_of) reaches it through _rename_in_proto_defaults (#4545) -- and then exposed the second half: Binder::_cur_refs re-scans a token whose text changed, and a Prototype fell to the interpolation arm and came back with NO refs, so @b's use in the OTHER default vanished, the capture promoter no longer promoted @b and the sub read an empty package @b (`f=/`).

=== DONE (s539b) ===
The port renames the default (a binder use); Binder::_proto_default_refs is the ONE reading of a one-token signature's defaults, at the build and at the re-scan.  Guard: Pl/t/rename-binder-01.t row 10 (fails on c1fe4930: `f=/8`).
subject: A default inside a ONE-TOKEN signature (Token::Prototype, #455) reading an exception-renamed file `my $a` read the special `$a` (the region walk never reached the token's text), and once a rename did reach it the binder re-read the token as interpolation and lost the OTHER defaults' uses -- pre-existing; fixed by 1c port 4 (s539b)
